title: To Heaven I Lift My Waiting Eyes
description: To Heaven I Lift My Waiting Eyes in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 121, part 2, headed “Preservation by day and night”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: To heaven I lift my wait-ing eyes, There all my hopes are laid: The Lord that built the earth and skies Is my per-pet-ual aid.

lines: To heaven I lift my waiting eyes,
There all my hopes are laid:
The Lord that built the earth and skies
Is my perpetual aid.
Their feet shall never slide to fall
Whom he designs to keep;
His ear attends the softest call,
His eyes can never sleep.
He will sustain our weakest powers
With his almighty arm,
And watch our most unguarded hours
Against surprising harm.
Israel, rejoice and rest secure,
Thy keeper is the Lord;
His wakeful eyes employ his power
For thine eternal guard.
Nor scorching sun, nor sickly moon,
Shall have his leave to smite;
He shields thy head from burning noon,
From blasting damps at night.
He guards thy soul, he keeps thy breath
Where thickest dangers come;
Go and return, secure from death,
Till God commands thee home.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
